rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act rent cap
rules.requirement: Landlords may not raise gross rent more than 5% plus local CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, in any 12-month period, and no more than two increases in that period. Initial rent for a new tenancy is not capped.
rules.quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower
rules.effective_date_note: Current version (SB 567) effective 2024-01-01 and operative 2024-04-01; original rule applied to rent increases on or after 2019-03-15.
rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted/subsidized affordable housing; school dormitories; housing under stricter local rent control; housing with a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years; separately alienable property (e.g., single-family homes, condos) if owner is not a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member and notice is given; owner-occupied duplex; mobilehome owners.
rules.interaction: Does not apply where a local rent control ordinance restricts annual increases to less than the state cap; not intended to expand or limit local authority under Civ. Code ch. 2.7 (§ 1954.50 et seq.).
rules.penalty: Civil action for injunctive relief, actual damages, attorney's fees, and up to 3x damages if willful; AG, city attorney or county counsel may enforce.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential real property statewide, except listed exemptions.

unverifiable_exemptions: separately alienable property (single-family homes, condos) owned by non-corporate/non-REIT owner with notice

rules.title: Just-cause exemption notice cross-reference in § 1947.12
rules.requirement: Owners of exempt separately alienable properties must give tenants written notice that the property is exempt from both the rent cap and the just cause requirements of Civ. Code § 1946.2. This section only references just cause and does not itself set eviction grounds.
rules.quoted_span: This property is not subject to the rent limits imposed by Section 1947.12 of the Civil Code and is not subject to the just cause requirements of Section 1946.2 of the Civil Code.
rules.interaction: Substantive just cause rules are in Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2, not in this document.

parsed.doc_summary: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12 (SB 567 version) sets the statewide rent cap of 5% + CPI (max 10%), operative 2024-04-01 and repealed 2030-01-01. It lists exemptions and says it yields to stricter local rent control. It only cross-references just cause (§ 1946.2).
